key_insight: Low-dimensional perovskite capping increases surface roughness while preserving or improving electronic uniformity, decoupling morphology from optoelectronic quality.
engineering_relevance: Mixed-dimensional capping offers a route to more durable perovskite photovoltaics without requiring smoother film surfaces.
method: Cap 3D perovskites with Ruddlesden–Popper layers derived from 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium.
Compare statistical AFM topography with spatially resolved confocal photoluminescence and quasi-Fermi level splitting.
Evaluate pristine and capped films under accelerated aging.
evidence_signal: Despite greater roughness, capped films showed enhanced photoluminescence, reduced non-radiative recombination, and more uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting, with better-preserved optoelectronic homogeneity during aging.
watch_item: The abstract does not report device-level efficiency, quantified aging conditions, or operational lifetime, so photovoltaic performance gains remain unverified here.
paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
